title: Joint anion-gap–bicarbonate information does not establish improved albuminuria prediction in cross-cycle NHANES validation
abstract: A frozen centered albumin-corrected anion-gap by bicarbonate interaction trained on 5,356 NHANES 2009–2010 adults and evaluated on 4,911 separately sampled 2015–2016 adults did not establish improved single-visit albuminuria prediction beyond routine kidney/metabolic variables and both main effects. Weighted Brier changed by −0.00000918 (95% fixed-model PSU-bootstrap interval −0.00024038 to +0.00019861). Penalty strength, sex strata and race-indicator removal changed the direction; adding standard eGFR reduced the point improvement further. Shared survey infrastructure, historical analyst exposure to these cycles, complete-case selection and single-visit labels limit confirmation and clinical interpretation. Raw public inputs, hashes, code, uncertainty calculations, unfavorable challenges and clean rerun evidence accompany this author-self-checked negative incremental-prediction test.
